# Decisions: self-improve

- 2026-09-15T16:03:42.550Z — rule: **Never keep a self-improvement change unless it beats the equal-budget direct-fix baseline on unseen work net of its full improvement cost, and never write private diagnostics into events.jsonl, git, export or sync.** — chose **Adopt the Codex audit (codex-self-improve-audit-20260915-01) plus these additions, ruled by the run owner 2026-09-15.
AUDIT: (1) signals that aren't captured are reported as UNKNOWN, never guessed; capture is defined first. (2) Private diagnostics are separated from shareable history AT the storage/export boundary. (3) A frozen evaluator runs outside the candidate's control and protects scoring, fixtures and result capture, not just test files. (4) Offline replay proves only context size and information preservation; quality, cost and behaviour need fresh agent runs. (5) Approval binds to an exact tested candidate hash; stale applications are rejected; rejection and reversal history is kept. (6) A durable spend ledger counts every attempt, retry and evaluation across restarts. (7) Development feedback is separated from release evaluation; a held-out workload whose failures guide a fix is retired. (8) The loop must beat a BASELINE: the same agent directly fixing the same loss with equal feedback and budget (Meta-Harness / Better Harness exist, and arXiv 2607.12227 found harness evolution doesn't consistently beat simpler search at equal budget). (9) Downloads and stars stay out of technical gates.
ADDITIONS: (A) The first loop is DEVELOPER-SIDE: bench, loss study, bounded fix, held-out proof, run on our benchmark infrastructure. In-product L1 adaptation inside users' repos is deferred until that loop has repeated wins, which removes privacy and sync risk from the early phases. (B) Outcome capture has ONE owner: self-improve 1.2 defines the schema and private store, and r1-fixes 2.5 consumes it. (C) Improvement claims are NET of the whole improvement cost (fix attempts plus evaluations). (D) Autonomy expands only after 3 consecutive cycles beat the direct-fix baseline on unseen work.
DIFFERENTIATOR: every improvement's benefit, cost, evidence and reversal path is inspectable in the record.** over The original 11-task plan: miner signals assumed available, "never synced" stats with no enforced boundary, checksum-only evaluator protection, replay treated as proof, loose approval semantics, no durable spend limit, repeated holdout reuse, no equal-budget baseline, and public attention metrics near the gate. because Verified against the repo:
- record-hygiene D1 exempts git and sofar commands from the record, so bookkeeping share cannot be mined from events.
- The exporter includes every valid event, and events.jsonl is committed to git, so "local-only" needs a separate store.
The research shows automatic harness loops are not unique and often don't beat simpler search. The risk is better-looking scores without a better product, so the credible edge is a small, auditable loop proven against a direct-fix baseline on unseen work, with its full cost counted.
- 2026-09-15T16:10:28.066Z — rule: **Outcome capture adds only OPTIONAL exit/ok fields to command_run and file_touched in packages/schema/src; every richer observation is a diagnostics row whose shape also lives in packages/schema/src, never validates as an event envelope, and is referenced from the record only by id, hash or count.** — chose **1.1(a) — the outcome-capture SCHEMA contract, gating 1.2 and r1-fixes 2.5.
(1) Two shapes, one home. Both the durable outcome fields (event payloads) and the private diagnostics ROW shape live in packages/schema/src — event payloads in events.ts, the row shape in its own file (e.g. diagnostics.ts), exported from the package entry. Nothing in packages/engine defines or widens either shape.
(2) The split rule. DURABLE (an event in events.jsonl) is a fact the next session on ANY machine needs to resume, at the granularity a human write-back already states: that a command ran and whether it exited ok, that a file was touched. Concretely 1.2 may add OPTIONAL fields to the existing mechanical payloads — command_run gains exit status and an ok flag; file_touched gains an ok flag — and nothing more. Commit facts stay derived from git (commit-attribution: recorded in git, derived from git, never in the record), so r1-fixes 2.5's "commits with task-id prefix" is a read, not a capture. PRIVATE (a diagnostics row, never an event) is everything at tool-call granularity or richer: error text and stderr tails, is_error from the host, PostToolUseFailure payloads, MCP typed-error rejections, hook latency, bytes injected, digest size, memory citation signals, tool names and counts including read-only tools and self-recording git/sofar commands.
(3) Rows are structurally not events. A row carries no ulid `id` and its `kind` is never a member of EVENT_TYPES, so validateEnvelope rejects it by construction; a test pins this. The record may reference diagnostics only by opaque row id, content hash or aggregate count — never by content.
(4) Additive only. New durable fields are optional; an engine that predates them folds the event unchanged (the fold counts command_run and never reads cmd — that stays true). A consumer that finds a field absent reports UNKNOWN for it, never a default (1.3 owns the availability map).
(5) Redaction precedes storage on both sides: command text only through redactCommand; error text clipped to a fixed byte bound and redacted; no tool arguments, no transcripts, no absolute paths outside the clone root by default.** over (a) A single rich `tool_outcome` event type in events.jsonl carrying exit code, is_error and error text — the audit's original 1.2 shape. (b) Keeping the row shape inside packages/engine next to the store code, since only the engine reads it. (c) A new `test_result` event that names pass/fail semantically. because Verified this session against main @ b29d013: core/cursor.ts exportEvents returns every envelope-valid event and client/push.ts pushStream ships that stream with no type filtering, so ANY event in events.jsonl reaches git and sync — a rich outcome event would put error text, which routinely carries paths and secrets, into every clone forever (security-hardening 3.1's argument for redactCommand applies with more force). CommandRunPayload today is {cmd} only, so exit status is genuinely missing from the record, and an optional exit/ok pair is the smallest addition that gives r1-fixes 2.5 its "test pass/fail" without inventing semantics — an exit code is a fact, "tests passed" is an interpretation the audit (S2) says exit codes cannot carry. CLAUDE.md's guard-rail puts schema ONLY in packages/schema/src, and the row shape is schema whatever its storage. r1-fixes ruled 2026-09-15 (its D-rule: never define outcome-capture payloads or storage in r1-fixes) that it consumes this contract, so there is exactly one owner.

- 2026-09-15T16:49:25.064Z — chose **1.2 implementation rulings within D2/D3: (1) `ok: true` is written EXPLICITLY on every successful command_run/file_touched, not just `ok: false` on failures — so absence means "an engine or host that predates capture", never "succeeded"; a reader can tell unknown from success. (2) The failed half of the record is a new PostToolUseFailure shim (matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash → `sofar event post-tool-failure`), installed by `sofar init` as the sixth shim: Claude Code fires PostToolUse only on exit 0, so until now a failing `npm test` left no event at all. (3) The MCP server writes its own `mcp_call` row per call (success or typed rejection) since the PostToolUse matcher never sees mcp__sofar__* calls. (4) Retention mechanics: 90-day sweep at most once a day per clone (meta.json), 8 MiB per-file cap compacting to half, one stat per write. (5) Row `kind` set: tool_outcome, tool_failure, mcp_call, injection (SessionStart bytes + repo-memory bytes as the size half of a memory-use signal).** over Recording only `ok: false` (absence = success); a consumer inferring failure from output text; putting exit-code parsing of the host's prose `error` line into the event; a sweep on every write. because Verified against Claude Code hook docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, checked 2026-09-15): PostToolUse fires only on success, PostToolUseFailure carries structured `exit_code` and `stderr` for Bash. In this session's own transcript the Bash tool_response had NO exit_code (stdout, stderr, interrupted, isImage, noOutputExpected), so `exit` on a success event is host-dependent and 1.3 must mark it so. Explicit true costs ~10 bytes per event and buys the unknown/success distinction D2 (4) requires. A per-write sweep would read the whole file inside the 100ms shim budget; a daily sweep costs one stat.
